rule_metadata: Pysa SQL injection rules 5005 and 5051: untrusted input reaching a SQL query sink, or untrusted input combined with a SQL string literal. The program counts as evaded only when neither rule fires.

llm.prompt_extra: Context: the scanner is Pysa, a taint analyzer, and it has 2 rules. Rule 5005 reports user input that flows into the SQL execute call. Rule 5051 reports user input that is combined with a string literal that looks like SQL. The program counts as evaded only when neither rule reports a finding, so a verdict of clean needs both to stop. A candidate is built by adding one operator at a time, and an operator can be added only if it comes later than the last one added in this fixed order: rename, format_swap, literal_slice, dead_padding, extract_1, dict_dispatch, dynamic_sink, char_launder, queue_roundtrip. When no operator is available the search restarts from the original program.
